ceiling_statement: For latency over a frozen workload distribution, the maximum assurance any H1–H8 system can provide is: (a) an EXACT, offline-verifiable deterministic cost certificate — for every workload item x, a cost value C(f,x) in abstract units (operations executed, bytes hashed, bytes consed, stage invocations) that any third party recomputes to bit-equality, so every quantile of the cost distribution over the frozen workload is a theorem, not a sample; plus (b) a fail-closed cost-budget gate that blocks any run whose certified cost exceeds a committed budget; plus (c) a wall-clock claim that is at most 'certified cost × attested machine rate r', where r is a signed measurement on declared hardware that is irreducibly attestation-trusted — no system can make wall-clock seconds themselves offline-verifiable with zero producer trust.
derivation: Two-part limit. (1) No-go on verified wall-clock: H5 requires trusted derivations to be pure functions of committed inputs, and H8 requires verification by recompute-and-compare. Wall-clock duration is not a function of committed inputs — it depends on scheduler interleaving, cache/thermal state, and hardware, so an independent verifier replaying the same committed inputs obtains a different number; recompute-and-compare over a non-recomputable quantity is undefined. Hence any wall-clock figure can only be a signed measurement (attested), never a zero-trust-verified fact; the offline-verifiable content of a latency claim is bounded above by what IS a pure function of inputs: the abstract cost of the deterministic execution path. (2) Exactness of the attainable part: because H5 makes the derivation deterministic, the multiset {C(f,x) : x ∈ frozen workload} is a computable function of the committed workload — its mean, p50, p99, and max are exactly computable and re-derivable by any verifier; statistical sampling error is eliminated entirely, which no measurement-based (non-frozen, non-pure) system can achieve. H3 then permits the strongest enforcement compatible with the no-go: a fail-closed budget gate on the certified cost (blocking, not advisory), while the seconds-conversion factor r remains a declared-resource attestation. Nothing feasible today exceeds this split: sublinear or hardware-independent verified timing would require either verified-hardware timing channels (not available) or trusting the producer's clock (violates H8).
attainment_mechanism: Buildable now in SBCL: (1) a deterministic cost meter at the existing single seats — count stage invocations and article units at systems/orchestrator-omega-modules/frbr-pipeline-stage.lisp, bytes hashed at source/hash-authority.lisp and source/merkle-authority.lisp, allocation via sb-ext:get-bytes-consed (already read by performance-metrics in systems/orchestrator-core/instrumentation.lisp) — all pure functions of the frozen input under H5; (2) a persisted, hash-chained latency/cost ledger reusing the [RATCHET-3] append-only SHA-256 chain pattern of source/memory.lisp, each entry = (workload-digest, cost-vector, wall-time, machine-fingerprint, Ed25519 signature via the source/authority-proof-bundle.lisp machinery), so cost claims are offline re-verifiable (H8) and wall-time is honestly attested-only; (3) a fail-closed budget gate as a CLOS :around barrier in the exact style of systems/orchestrator-cli/constitutional-dispatch.lisp, refusing (H3) any command whose certified cost exceeds the committed budget; (4) exact quantile computation over the frozen workload emitted as a verifiable artifact through the gate-plenary manifest pattern of systems/orchestrator-cli/gates-runner.lisp.
b0_gap: The B0 map (§4, honest note) records AX-17 as effectively ABSENT — the sole evidence is systems/orchestrator-core/instrumentation.lisp + executor metrics: in-memory wall-clock timing (get-internal-real-time) that gates nothing, enforces no budget, is discarded on context cleanup, and carries two ad-hoc logging seats (log-info/log-error, a 'replacement for log4cl'). Verified in-repo: with-instrumentation writes only to *trace-output* and the transient context. Gap to ceiling: no deterministic cost measure (wall-clock only, hence nothing replayable), no persisted ledger, no budget gate, no signed machine attestation, no exact workload quantiles. Every ingredient (hash chain, Ed25519, :around gate, manifest) already has a B0 seat; the cost meter and ledger are new but mechanically small.
lean_obligation: Theorem (cost determinism and exact quantiles): given `f : Input → Output` with `Pure f` (no clock/RNG/IO), there exists a unique `c : Input → ℕ` such that for all executions `e` of `f` on `x`, `cost e = c x`; consequently for a frozen workload `w : Multiset Input`, `quantile q (w.map c)` is a computable function of `w` alone, and two independent replays yield equal quantile vectors. No-go lemma: there is no function `V : CommittedInputs → ℝ` with `V = wallClock` unless `wallClock` is constant across conforming executions — i.e., wall-clock latency is not offline-verifiable under H5/H8; any latency bound decomposes as `latency ≤ c x * r` with `r` an attested constant outside the verified kernel. Budget gate soundness: `∀ x, c x > budget → executes f x = blocked` (fail-closed, H3).
